comparisons.peer_summary: BANA is able to declare and pay dividends of approximately $13.0 billion to the Corporation in 2025, plus an additional amount equal to its retained net profits for 2025 up to the date of any such declaration.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose the specific capacity of their primary banking subsidiaries to pay dividends to the parent holding company without prior regulatory approval, supplemented by current-year earnings. JPM estimates this capacity at approximately $15.5 billion at January 1, 2025, while BANA estimates it at approximately $13.0 billion for 2025.

sentences.text: At January 1, 2025, the Parent Company's banking subsidiaries could pay, in the aggregate, approximately $15.5 billion in dividends to their respective bank holding companies without the prior approval of their relevant banking regulators.
The capacity to pay dividends in 2025 will be supplemented by the banking subsidiaries' earnings during the year.

In 2025, BANA can declare and pay dividends of approximately $13.0 billion to the Corporation plus an additional amount equal to its retained net profits for 2025 up to the date of any such dividend declaration.

comparisons.peer_summary: Group Inc. may be limited in accessing capital at subsidiaries due to regulatory, tax, or other constraints, including laws requiring prior regulatory approval for dividends. For example, GS Bank USA's dividend payments are capped by earnings and undivided profits tests.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss regulatory constraints on accessing capital from subsidiaries via dividends. JPM explicitly quantifies the amount available without approval ($15.5 billion), while GS describes the structural limitations (earnings and undivided profits tests) that cap dividend payments by its primary subsidiary, GS Bank USA, without providing a specific aggregate dollar figure for 2024 capacity.

sentences.text: At January 1, 2025, the Parent Company's banking subsidiaries could pay, in the aggregate, approximately $15.5 billion in dividends to their respective bank holding companies without the prior approval of their relevant banking regulators.
The capacity to pay dividends in 2025 will be supplemented by the banking subsidiaries' earnings during the year.

These limitations include provisions of applicable law and regulations and other regulatory restrictions that limit the ability of those subsidiaries to declare and pay dividends without prior regulatory approval.
For example, the amount of dividends that may be paid by GS Bank USA are limited to the lesser of the amounts calculated under a recent earnings test and an undivided profits test.
